decoys.mutated_claim: A DPIA is required for systematic and extensive evaluation of personal aspects of natural persons based on automated processing including profiling where decisions with legal or similarly significant effects are based on such processing only if consent is obtained.
A data protection impact assessment is required when processing is likely to result in a low risk to the rights and freedoms of data subjects.
Processing should be screened for factors indicating high-risk processing, such as processing data of non-vulnerable individuals.
Innovative technology refers to new developments in technological knowledge only to the controller rather than technology that is new at large.
Extensive processing implies that the processing covers a large area, involves a wide range of data, and affects a large number of individuals.
In most cases, a combination of three factors from the WP29 criteria indicates the need for a DPIA, though this is not a strict rule.
The ICO will acknowledge receipt of a DPIA submission and notify the applicant within 5 days whether the DPIA has been accepted for prior consultation.
The ICO must be consulted if a DPIA identifies a high risk that can be mitigated through measures.
DPIAs should be kept under review and revisited on a quarterly basis.
The ICO requires DPIAs for use of innovative technology or criteria from European guidelines.
If high risk is accepted because mitigation is impossible or costs are too high, ICO consultation is optional before processing proceeds.
A DPIA may relate to a single data processing operation or can evaluate several dissimilar processing operations in terms of nature, scope, context, purposes and risks.

A DPIA submission to the ICO must include descriptions of roles and responsibilities of joint controllers or processors, processing purposes and methods, protective measures and safeguards, DPO contact details, and a copy of the Data Protection Impact Assessment summary.
Organizations should consult only individuals when carrying out a DPIA.
The DPC will respond to a prior consultation submission within four weeks if the processing would infringe GDPR provisions or risks are insufficiently identified or mitigated.
DPIAs are relevant to Data Protection Officers and those with specific data protection responsibilities in smaller organisations.
Legal advice or advice from independent experts such as IT experts, sociologists or ethicists must be considered where appropriate, with specific requirements to do so.
Employees may be considered vulnerable data subjects where a power imbalance means they can easily consent or object to data processing by an employer.
Harm does not have to be inevitable to qualify as high risk; it must be more than certain, but any significant possibility of very serious harm may still qualify as high risk.
The DPC response period may be extended by up to twelve weeks to account for the complexity of the proposed processing.

extractions.quote: A single assessment may address a set of similar processing operations that present similar high risks.

extractions.assertion: The data protection officer must be consulted when carrying out a data protection impact assessment if one has been designated.
extractions.quote: The controller shall seek the advice of the data protection officer, where designated, when carrying out a data protection impact assessment.

extractions.assertion: A DPIA is required for systematic and extensive evaluation of personal aspects of natural persons based on automated processing including profiling where decisions with legal or similarly significant effects are based on such processing.
extractions.quote: a systematic and extensive evaluation of personal aspects relating to natural persons which is based on automated processing, including profiling, and on which decisions are based that produce legal effects concerning the natural person or similarly significantly affect the natural person

extractions.quote: a systematic description of the envisaged processing operations and the purposes of the processing, including, where applicable, the legitimate interest pursued by the controller

extractions.quote: an assessment of the necessity and proportionality of the processing operations in relation to the purposes

extractions.assertion: A DPIA must contain an assessment of the risks to the rights and freedoms of data subjects.
extractions.quote: an assessment of the risks to the rights and freedoms of data subjects referred to in paragraph 1

extractions.assertion: A DPIA must describe the measures envisaged to address risks, including safeguards, security measures and mechanisms to ensure the protection of personal data and demonstrate compliance with the Regulation.
extractions.quote: the measures envisaged to address the risks, including safeguards, security measures and mechanisms to ensure the protection of personal data and to demonstrate compliance with this Regulation taking into account the rights and legitimate interests of data subjects and other persons concerned

extractions.assertion: Compliance with approved codes of conduct by controllers or processors shall be taken into due account when assessing the impact of processing operations in a data protection impact assessment.
extractions.quote: Compliance with approved codes of conduct referred to in Article 40 by the relevant controllers or processors shall be taken into due account in assessing the impact of the processing operations performed by such controllers or processors, in particular for the purposes of a data protection impact assessment.

extractions.assertion: The controller should seek the views of data subjects or their representatives on the intended processing when appropriate, without prejudice to the protection of commercial or public interests or the security of processing operations.
extractions.quote: Where appropriate, the controller shall seek the views of data subjects or their representatives on the intended processing, without prejudice to the protection of commercial or public interests or the security of processing operations.

extractions.assertion: When a data protection impact assessment has already been carried out as part of a general impact assessment required by domestic law for processing pursuant to points (c) or (e) of Article 6(1), the DPIA requirements do not apply unless domestic law provides otherwise.
extractions.quote: In the case of processing pursuant to point (c) or (e) of Article 6(1), paragraphs 1 to 7 of this Article do not apply if a data protection impact assessment has already been carried out for the processing as part of a general impact assessment required by domestic law, unless domestic law provides otherwise.

extractions.assertion: A controller shall carry out a review to assess if processing is performed in accordance with the data protection impact assessment at least when there is a change of the risk represented by processing operations.
extractions.quote: Where necessary, the controller shall carry out a review to assess if processing is performed in accordance with the data protection impact assessment at least when there is a change of the risk represented by processing operations.

extractions.assertion: A Data Protection Impact Assessment must be conducted when a type of processing, particularly involving new technologies and considering the nature, scope, context and purposes, is likely to result in high risk to the rights and freedoms of individuals.
extractions.quote: Article 35(1) says that you must do a DPIA where a type of processing is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of individuals: 'Where a type of processing in particular using new technologies, and taking into account the nature, scope, context and purposes of the processing, is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons, the controller shall, prior to the processing, carry out an assessment of the impact of the envisaged processing operations on the protection of personal data.'

extractions.assertion: High risk means potential for any significant physical, material or non-material harm to individuals, assessed by considering both the likelihood and severity of potential harm.
extractions.quote: Risk in this context is about the potential for any significant physical, material or non-material harm to individuals. To assess whether something is 'high risk', the UK GDPR is clear that you need to consider both the likelihood and severity of any potential harm to individuals.

extractions.assertion: The screening test for likely high risk involves identifying red flags that indicate potential high risk rather than assessing whether processing is actually high risk.
extractions.quote: Instead, the question is a more high-level screening test: are there features which point to the potential for high risk? You are screening for any red flags which indicate that you need to do a DPIA to look at the risk (including the likelihood and severity of potential harm) in more detail.

extractions.assertion: Systematic and extensive profiling with significant effects automatically requires a DPIA under Article 35(3).
extractions.quote: Article 35(3) sets out three types of processing which always require a DPIA: Systematic and extensive profiling with significant effects: '(a) any systematic and extensive evaluation of personal aspects relating to natural persons which is based on automated processing, including profiling, and on which decisions are based that produce legal effects concerning the natural person or similarly significantly affect the natural person.'

extractions.assertion: Large-scale processing of special category data or personal data relating to criminal convictions automatically requires a DPIA under Article 35(3).
extractions.quote: Large scale use of sensitive data: '(b) processing on a large scale of special categories of data referred to in Article 9(1), or of personal data relating to criminal convictions and offences referred to in Article 10.'

extractions.assertion: Large-scale systematic monitoring of publicly accessible areas automatically requires a DPIA under Article 35(3).
extractions.quote: Public monitoring: '(c) a systematic monitoring of a publicly accessible area on a large scale.'

extractions.assertion: In most cases, a combination of two factors from the WP29 high-risk indicators points to the need for a DPIA, but this is not an absolute rule.
extractions.quote: In most cases, a combination of two of these factors indicates the need for a DPIA. However, this is not a strict rule. You may be able to justify a decision not to carry out a DPIA if you are confident that the processing is nevertheless unlikely to result in a high risk, but you should document your reasons.

extractions.assertion: Innovative technology refers to new developments in technological knowledge in the world at large, rather than technology that is new to the individual organization.
extractions.quote: Recital 91 says innovative technology concerns new developments in technological knowledge in the world at large, rather than technology that is new to you, and its use can trigger the need to carry out a DPIA.

extractions.assertion: Systematic processing means processing that occurs according to a system, is pre-arranged and organized, takes place as part of a general plan, or is carried out as part of a strategy.
extractions.quote: The DPO guidelines say that 'systematic' means that the processing: occurs according to a system; is pre-arranged, organised or methodical; takes place as part of a general plan for data collection; or is carried out as part of a strategy.

extractions.assertion: Extensive processing implies that the processing covers a large area, involves a wide range of data, or affects a large number of individuals.
extractions.quote: The term 'extensive' implies that the processing also covers a large area, involves a wide range of data or affects a large number of individuals.

extractions.assertion: A legal or similarly significant effect is something that has a noticeable impact on an individual and can significantly affect their circumstances, behaviour or choices.
extractions.quote: In short, it is something that has a noticeable impact on an individual and can significantly affect their circumstances, behaviour or choices. A legal effect is something that affects a person's legal status or legal rights.

extractions.assertion: Invisible processing occurs when personal data is obtained from sources other than the data subject directly without providing Article 14 privacy information.
extractions.quote: 'Invisible processing' occurs when you obtain personal data from somewhere other than directly from the individual themselves, and you don't provide them with the privacy information required by Article 14. The processing is 'invisible' because the individual is unaware that you are collecting and using their personal data, even if you publish a privacy notice on your website.

extractions.assertion: A DPIA is required for invisible processing when combined with any of the criteria from the European guidelines.
extractions.quote: Invisible processing: processing of personal data that has not been obtained direct from the data subject in circumstances where the controller considers that compliance with Article 14 would prove impossible or involve disproportionate effort. A DPIA is required where this processing is combined with any of the criteria from the European guidelines.

extractions.assertion: Vulnerable individuals are those whose circumstances may restrict their ability to freely consent or object to processing or understand its implications.
extractions.quote: Individuals can be vulnerable where circumstances may restrict their ability to freely consent or object to the processing of their personal data, or to understand its implications.

extractions.assertion: Children are regarded as vulnerable because they may be less able to understand how their data is used, anticipate effects, and protect themselves from consequences.
extractions.quote: Most obviously, children are regarded as vulnerable to the processing of their personal data since they may be less able to understand how their data is being used, anticipate how this might affect them, and protect themselves against any unwanted consequences.

extractions.assertion: Employees may be considered vulnerable data subjects where a power imbalance means they cannot easily consent or object to processing by an employer.
extractions.quote: The European guidelines on DPIAs (WP248) explain why employees could be considered vulnerable data subjects where a power imbalance means they cannot easily consent or object to the processing of their data by an employer.

extractions.assertion: Large-scale processing should be assessed by considering the number of individuals, volume of data, variety of data, duration of processing, and geographical extent.
extractions.quote: to decide whether processing is on a large scale you should consider: the number of individuals concerned; the volume of data; the variety of data; the duration of the processing; and the geographical extent of the processing.

extractions.assertion: A hospital processing patient data constitutes large-scale processing, but an individual doctor is not.
extractions.quote: Examples of large-scale processing include: a hospital (but not an individual doctor) processing patient data; tracking individuals using a city's public transport system; a fast food chain tracking real-time location of its customers; an insurance company or bank processing customer data; a search engine processing data for behavioural advertising; or a telephone or internet service provider processing user data. Individual professionals processing patient or client data are not processing on a large scale.

extractions.assertion: An exception to DPIA requirements applies when processing is based on legal obligation or public task if specific conditions are met.
extractions.quote: You may not have to carry out a DPIA if: You are processing on the basis of legal obligation or public task. However, this exception only applies if: you are not subject to other obligations to complete DPIAs derived from specific legislation, such as Digital Economy Act 2017; you have a clear statutory basis for the processing; the legal provision or a statutory code specifically provides for and regulates the processing operation in question; and a data protection risk assessment was carried out as part of the impact assessment when the legislation was adopted.

extractions.assertion: A DPIA exception applies when substantially similar DPIA has already been completed for processing with similar nature, scope, context and purposes.
extractions.quote: You have already done a substantially similar DPIA. You need to be confident that you can demonstrate that the nature, scope, context and purposes of the processing are all similar.

extractions.assertion: Innovative technology requires a DPIA in combination with another criterion from European guidelines according to the ICO list.
extractions.quote: The ICO list of high-risk processing operations requires a DPIA if your processing involves innovative technology in combination with another criterion from the European guidelines (e.g. evaluation or scoring, or sensitive data).

extractions.assertion: If processing involves invisible processing combined with any vulnerable individuals or other criteria, a DPIA must be conducted to help assess and mitigate impact on individuals' ability to exercise control over their data.
extractions.quote: Your DPIA will help you assess and demonstrate whether you are taking a proportionate approach. It will help you consider how best to mitigate the impact on individuals' ability to exercise control over their data, and whether you can take other measures to support the exercise of their rights.

extractions.quote: A data protection impact assessment referred to in paragraph 1 shall in particular be required in the case of: (a)a systematic and extensive evaluation of personal aspects relating to natural persons which is based on automated processing, including profiling, and on which decisions are based that produce legal effects concerning the natural person or similarly significantly affect the natural person

extractions.assertion: Controllers must seek advice from the data protection officer when one is designated while carrying out a data protection impact assessment.
extractions.quote: The controller shall seek the advice of the data protection officer, where designated, when carrying out a data protection impact assessment.

extractions.assertion: A data protection impact assessment must contain a systematic description of the envisaged processing operations and purposes, including the legitimate interest pursued by the controller where applicable.
extractions.quote: The assessment shall contain at least: (a)a systematic description of the envisaged processing operations and the purposes of the processing, including, where applicable, the legitimate interest pursued by the controller

extractions.assertion: A data protection impact assessment must include an assessment of the necessity and proportionality of the processing operations in relation to the purposes.
extractions.quote: (b)an assessment of the necessity and proportionality of the processing operations in relation to the purposes

extractions.assertion: A data protection impact assessment must include an assessment of the risks to the rights and freedoms of data subjects.
extractions.quote: (c)an assessment of the risks to the rights and freedoms of data subjects referred to in paragraph 1

extractions.assertion: A data protection impact assessment must document the measures envisaged to address risks including safeguards, security measures and mechanisms to ensure protection and demonstrate compliance.
extractions.quote: (d)the measures envisaged to address the risks, including safeguards, security measures and mechanisms to ensure the protection of personal data and to demonstrate compliance with this Regulation taking into account the rights and legitimate interests of data subjects and other persons concerned.

extractions.assertion: Supervisory authorities must establish and publicly list the kinds of processing operations subject to data protection impact assessment requirements.
extractions.quote: The supervisory authority shall establish and make public a list of the kind of processing operations which are subject to the requirement for a data protection impact assessment pursuant to paragraph 1.

extractions.assertion: Supervisory authorities may establish and publicly list the kinds of processing operations for which no data protection impact assessment is required.
extractions.quote: The supervisory authority may also establish and make public a list of the kind of processing operations for which no data protection impact assessment is required.

extractions.assertion: When processing has legal basis in Union law or Member State law that regulates the specific operation and a data protection impact assessment has already been carried out as part of a general impact assessment, the assessment paragraphs do not apply unless the Member State deems it necessary.
extractions.quote: Where processing pursuant to point (c) or (e) of Article 6(1) has a legal basis in Union law or in the law of the Member State to which the controller is subject, that law regulates the specific processing operation or set of operations in question, and a data protection impact assessment has already been carried out as part of a general impact assessment in the context of the adoption of that legal basis, paragraphs 1 to 7 shall not apply unless Member States deem it to be necessary.

extractions.assertion: Controllers should seek views of data subjects or their representatives on intended processing when appropriate, without prejudice to protection of commercial interests, public interests or security of operations.
extractions.quote: Where appropriate, the controller shall seek the views of data subjects or their representatives on the intended processing, without prejudice to the protection of commercial or public interests or the security of processing operations.

extractions.assertion: Controllers must conduct a review to assess if processing complies with the data protection impact assessment when there is a change in the risk represented by processing operations.
extractions.quote: Where necessary, the controller shall carry out a review to assess if processing is performed in accordance with the data protection impact assessment at least when there is a change of the risk represented by processing operations.

extractions.assertion: A Data Protection Impact Assessment must be conducted when a type of processing is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of individuals.
extractions.quote: Article 35(1) says that you must do a DPIA where a type of processing is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of individuals

extractions.assertion: High risk in the context of DPIAs refers to the potential for any significant physical, material or non-material harm to individuals.
extractions.quote: Risk in this context is about the potential for any significant physical, material or non-material harm to individuals.

extractions.assertion: Assessing whether something qualifies as high risk requires considering both the likelihood and severity of any potential harm to individuals.
extractions.quote: To assess whether something is 'high risk', the UK GDPR is clear that you need to consider both the likelihood and severity of any potential harm to individuals.

extractions.assertion: The screening test for whether processing is likely to result in high risk focuses on identifying red flags that indicate potential high risk rather than assessing actual harm.
extractions.quote: You are screening for any red flags which indicate that you need to do a DPIA to look at the risk (including the likelihood and severity of potential harm) in more detail.

extractions.assertion: Three types of processing automatically require a DPIA: systematic and extensive profiling with significant effects, large scale use of sensitive data, and public monitoring.
extractions.quote: Article 35(3) sets out three types of processing which always require a DPIA: Systematic and extensive profiling with significant effects... Large scale use of sensitive data... Public monitoring

extractions.assertion: Processing involving evaluation or scoring of personal aspects is identified as an indicator of likely high-risk processing.
extractions.quote: The Article 29 working party of EU data protection authorities (WP29) published guidelines with nine criteria which may act as indicators of likely high risk processing: Evaluation or scoring.

extractions.assertion: Automated decision-making with legal or similarly significant effect is identified as an indicator of likely high-risk processing.
extractions.quote: The Article 29 working party of EU data protection authorities (WP29) published guidelines with nine criteria which may act as indicators of likely high risk processing... Automated decision-making with legal or similar significant effect.

extractions.assertion: In most cases, a combination of two factors from the WP29 criteria indicates the need for a DPIA, though this is not a strict rule.
extractions.quote: In most cases, a combination of two of these factors indicates the need for a DPIA. However, this is not a strict rule.

extractions.assertion: Processing involving innovative technologies requires a DPIA when combined with any criteria from the European guidelines.
extractions.quote: Innovative technology: processing involving the use of innovative technologies, or the novel application of existing technologies (including AI). A DPIA is required where this processing is combined with any of the criteria from the European guidelines.

extractions.assertion: Innovative technology refers to new developments in technological knowledge at large rather than technology that is new only to the controller.
extractions.quote: Recital 91 says innovative technology concerns new developments in technological knowledge in the world at large, rather than technology that is new to you

extractions.assertion: Artificial intelligence, machine learning, autonomous vehicles, and smart technologies are examples of innovative technologies that can trigger DPIA requirements.
extractions.quote: Examples of processing using innovative technology include: artificial intelligence, machine learning and deep learning; connected and autonomous vehicles; intelligent transport systems; smart technologies (including wearables)

extractions.assertion: Processing is systematic when it occurs according to a system, is pre-arranged or methodical, and takes place as part of a general plan for data collection.
extractions.quote: The DPO guidelines say that 'systematic' means that the processing: occurs according to a system; is pre-arranged, organised or methodical; takes place as part of a general plan for data collection

extractions.assertion: Extensive processing covers a large area, involves a wide range of data, or affects a large number of individuals.
extractions.quote: The term 'extensive' implies that the processing also covers a large area, involves a wide range of data or affects a large number of individuals.

extractions.assertion: A legal effect is something that affects a person's legal status or legal rights.
extractions.quote: A legal effect is something that affects a person's legal status or legal rights.

extractions.assertion: A similarly significant effect to legal effects includes impacts on financial status, health, reputation, access to services or economic or social opportunities.
extractions.quote: A similarly significant effect might include something that affects a person's financial status, health, reputation, access to services or other economic or social opportunities.

extractions.assertion: Invisible processing occurs when personal data is obtained from sources other than directly from the individual and privacy information required by Article 14 is not provided.
extractions.quote: 'Invisible processing' occurs when you obtain personal data from somewhere other than directly from the individual themselves, and you don't provide them with the privacy information required by Article 14.

extractions.assertion: Invisible processing requires a DPIA when combined with any criteria from the European guidelines.
extractions.quote: Invisible processing: processing of personal data that has not been obtained direct from the data subject in circumstances where the controller considers that compliance with Article 14 would prove impossible or involve disproportionate effort. A DPIA is required where this processing is combined with any of the criteria from the European guidelines.

extractions.assertion: Vulnerable individuals are those whose circumstances may restrict their ability to freely consent or object to data processing or understand its implications.
extractions.quote: Individuals can be vulnerable where circumstances may restrict their ability to freely consent or object to the processing of their personal data, or to understand its implications.

extractions.assertion: Children are regarded as vulnerable to the processing of their personal data because they may be less able to understand how their data is being used and protect themselves.
extractions.quote: Most obviously, children are regarded as vulnerable to the processing of their personal data since they may be less able to understand how their data is being used, anticipate how this might affect them, and protect themselves against any unwanted consequences.

extractions.assertion: An imbalance of power in a relationship can cause vulnerability for data protection purposes if individuals believe they will be disadvantaged if processing does not go ahead.
extractions.quote: Even if the individuals are not part of a group you might automatically consider vulnerable, an imbalance of power in their relationship with you can cause vulnerability for data protection purposes if they believe that they will be disadvantaged if the processing doesn't go ahead.

extractions.assertion: Employees may be considered vulnerable data subjects where a power imbalance means they cannot easily consent or object to data processing by an employer.
extractions.quote: One group who may count as vulnerable in this sense are employees. The European guidelines on DPIAs (WP248) explain why employees could be considered vulnerable data subjects where a power imbalance means they cannot easily consent or object to the processing of their data by an employer.

extractions.assertion: To determine whether processing is on a large scale, one should consider the number of individuals concerned, volume of data, variety of data, duration of processing, and geographical extent.
extractions.quote: to decide whether processing is on a large scale you should consider: the number of individuals concerned; the volume of data; the variety of data; the duration of the processing; and the geographical extent of the processing.

extractions.assertion: Hospitals processing patient data are examples of large-scale processing, whereas individual doctors are not.
extractions.quote: Examples of large-scale processing include: a hospital (but not an individual doctor) processing patient data

extractions.assertion: A DPIA may not be required if processing is based on legal obligation or public task and certain conditions are met regarding statutory basis and prior risk assessment.
extractions.quote: You may not have to carry out a DPIA if: You are processing on the basis of legal obligation or public task. However, this exception only applies if: you are not subject to other obligations to complete DPIAs derived from specific legislation, such as Digital Economy Act 2017; you have a clear statutory basis for the processing

extractions.assertion: A DPIA is not required if a substantially similar DPIA has already been completed with the same nature, scope, context and purposes of processing.
extractions.quote: You have already done a substantially similar DPIA. You need to be confident that you can demonstrate that the nature, scope, context and purposes of the processing are all similar.

extractions.assertion: When processing involves the use of data obtained from third parties, controllers must carefully consider whether they can provide privacy information to individuals.
extractions.quote: If you are proposing processing operations that involve the use of data obtained from third parties, you must first carefully consider whether you can provide privacy information to the individuals.

extractions.assertion: When relying on the disproportionate effort exception for not providing privacy information, controllers must be able to justify this and take other measures to protect people's rights.
extractions.quote: If you intend to rely on the exception for disproportionate effort, you must be able to justify this, and you must take other measures to protect people's rights.

extractions.assertion: A Data Protection Impact Assessment is a process designed to help organizations identify and minimize data protection risks associated with a project.
extractions.quote: A Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) is a process to help you identify and minimise the data protection risks of a project.

extractions.assertion: Organizations must conduct a DPIA for processing that is likely to result in high risk to individuals, including certain specified types of processing.
extractions.quote: You must do a DPIA for processing that is likely to result in a high risk to individuals. This includes some specified types of processing.

extractions.assertion: A DPIA must include description of the nature, scope, context and purposes of the processing, assessment of necessity and proportionality, identification and assessment of risks, and identification of additional mitigation measures.
extractions.quote: Your DPIA must: describe the nature, scope, context and purposes of the processing; assess necessity, proportionality and compliance measures; identify and assess risks to individuals; and identify any additional measures to mitigate those risks.

extractions.assertion: Risk assessment in a DPIA must consider both the likelihood and the severity of potential impacts on individuals.
extractions.quote: To assess the level of risk, you must consider both the likelihood and the severity of any impact on individuals.

extractions.assertion: Consultation with data protection officers and where appropriate with individuals and relevant experts is a requirement in the DPIA process.
extractions.quote: You should consult your data protection officer (if you have one) and, where appropriate, individuals and relevant experts.

extractions.assertion: Processors may need to assist in the DPIA process by helping understand and document their processing activities and identify associated risks.
extractions.quote: Any processors may also need to assist you.

extractions.assertion: If a high risk cannot be mitigated, the organization must consult the ICO before starting the processing.
extractions.quote: If you identify a high risk that you cannot mitigate, you must consult the ICO before starting the processing.

extractions.assertion: Organizations must always conduct a DPIA if they plan to use systematic and extensive profiling or automated decision-making to make significant decisions about people.
extractions.quote: We always carry out a DPIA if we plan to: use systematic and extensive profiling or automated decision-making to make significant decisions about people

extractions.assertion: Organizations must always conduct a DPIA if they plan to process special-category data or criminal-offence data on a large scale.
extractions.quote: We always carry out a DPIA if we plan to: process special-category data or criminal-offence data on a large scale

extractions.assertion: Organizations must always conduct a DPIA if they plan to systematically monitor a publicly accessible place on a large scale.
extractions.quote: We always carry out a DPIA if we plan to: systematically monitor a publicly accessible place on a large scale

extractions.assertion: Organizations must always conduct a DPIA if they plan to use profiling, automated decision-making or special category data to help make decisions on someone's access to a service, opportunity or benefit.
extractions.quote: We always carry out a DPIA if we plan to: use profiling, automated decision-making or special category data to help make decisions on someone's access to a service, opportunity or benefit

extractions.assertion: Organizations must always conduct a DPIA if they plan to carry out profiling on a large scale.
extractions.quote: We always carry out a DPIA if we plan to: carry out profiling on a large scale

extractions.assertion: Organizations must always conduct a DPIA if they plan to process personal data without providing a privacy notice directly to the individual in combination with any criteria from European guidelines.
extractions.quote: We always carry out a DPIA if we plan to: process personal data without providing a privacy notice directly to the individual in combination with any of the criteria in the European guidelines

extractions.assertion: Organizations must always conduct a DPIA if they plan to process personal data that involves tracking individuals' online or offline location or behaviour in combination with criteria from European guidelines.
extractions.quote: We always carry out a DPIA if we plan to: process personal data in a way that involves tracking individuals' online or offline location or behaviour, in combination with any of the criteria in the European guidelines

extractions.assertion: Organizations must always conduct a DPIA if they plan to process children's personal data for profiling, automated decision-making, marketing purposes, or offer online services directly to them.
extractions.quote: We always carry out a DPIA if we plan to: process children's personal data for profiling or automated decision-making or for marketing purposes, or offer online services directly to them

extractions.assertion: Organizations must always conduct a DPIA if they plan to process personal data that could result in a risk of physical harm in the event of a security breach.
extractions.quote: We always carry out a DPIA if we plan to: process personal data that could result in a risk of physical harm in the event of a security breach.

extractions.assertion: It is good practice to conduct a DPIA for any major project involving the processing of personal data even if not legally required.
extractions.quote: It is also good practice to do a DPIA for any other major project which requires the processing of personal data.

extractions.assertion: A new DPIA should be carried out if there is a change to the nature, scope, context or purposes of processing.
extractions.quote: We carry out a new DPIA if there is a change to the nature, scope, context or purposes of our processing.

extractions.assertion: If an organization decides not to carry out a DPIA, the decision and its reasons must be documented.
extractions.quote: If we decide not to carry out a DPIA, we document our reasons.

extractions.assertion: Organizations should seek advice from their data protection officer during the DPIA process.
extractions.quote: We ask for the advice of our data protection officer.

extractions.assertion: Organizations should consult individuals and other relevant stakeholders when carrying out a DPIA.
extractions.quote: We consider how best to consult individuals (or their representatives) and other relevant stakeholders.

extractions.assertion: A DPIA must objectively assess the likelihood and severity of any risks to individuals' rights and interests.
extractions.quote: We do an objective assessment of the likelihood and severity of any risks to individuals' rights and interests.

extractions.assertion: Organizations must identify and document measures to eliminate or reduce high risks identified in a DPIA.
extractions.quote: We identify measures we can put in place to eliminate or reduce high risks.

extractions.assertion: Decision-making within a DPIA, including any difference of opinion with the DPO or individuals consulted, must be recorded in the DPIA outcome.
extractions.quote: We record our decision-making in the outcome of the DPIA, including any difference of opinion with our DPO or individuals consulted.

extractions.assertion: Measures identified in a DPIA should be implemented and integrated into the project plan.
extractions.quote: We implement the measures we identified, and integrate them into our project plan.

extractions.assertion: DPIAs should be kept under review and revisited when necessary.
extractions.quote: We keep our DPIAs under review and revisit them when necessary.

extractions.assertion: A well-written DPIA should explain why a DPIA was needed and detail the types of intended processing that made it a requirement.
extractions.quote: We have: explained why we needed a DPIA, detailing the types of intended processing that made it a requirement

extractions.assertion: A DPIA should clearly state how the organization is complying with each of the Data Protection Principles under GDPR and explain the lawful basis for processing.
extractions.quote: We have: explicitly stated how we are complying with each of the Data Protection Principles under GDPR and clearly explained our lawful basis for processing

extractions.assertion: A DPIA should identify all relevant risks to individuals' rights and freedoms, assess their likelihood and severity, and detail all relevant mitigations.
extractions.quote: We have: identified all relevant risks to individuals' rights and freedoms, assessed their likelihood and severity, and detailed all relevant mitigations

extractions.assertion: A DPIA should explain how proposed mitigation measures reduce the identified risks.
extractions.quote: We have: explained sufficiently how any proposed mitigation reduces the identified risk in question

extractions.assertion: A DPIA should evidence consideration of less risky alternatives to achieving the same purposes and explain why they were not chosen.
extractions.quote: We have: evidenced our consideration of any less risky alternatives to achieving the same purposes of the processing, and why we didn't choose them

extractions.assertion: A DPIA should include details of stakeholder consultation and summaries of findings.
extractions.quote: We have: given details of stakeholder consultation (e.g. data subjects, representative bodies) and included summaries of findings

extractions.assertion: The advice and recommendations of the DPO should be recorded in a DPIA where relevant and the DPIA should be signed off by appropriate people.
extractions.quote: We have: recorded the advice and recommendations of our DPO (where relevant) and ensured the DPIA is signed off by the appropriate people

extractions.assertion: A schedule for regularly reviewing the DPIA or reviewing it when processing changes should be agreed and documented.
extractions.quote: We have: agreed and documented a schedule for reviewing the DPIA regularly or when we change the nature, scope, context or purposes of the processing

extractions.assertion: Organizations must consult the ICO if there are residual high risks that cannot be mitigated.
extractions.quote: We have: consulted the ICO if there are residual high risks we cannot mitigate.

extractions.assertion: A DPIA is a systematic and comprehensive analysis of processing activities designed to identify and minimize data protection risks.
extractions.quote: A DPIA is a way for you to systematically and comprehensively analyse your processing and help you identify and minimise data protection risks.

extractions.assertion: DPIAs should consider compliance risks as well as broader risks to individual rights and freedoms, including potential for significant social or economic disadvantage.
extractions.quote: DPIAs should consider compliance risks, but also broader risks to the rights and freedoms of individuals, including the potential for any significant social or economic disadvantage.

extractions.assertion: A DPIA does not require eradication of all risks but should help document risks and assess whether any remaining risks are justified.
extractions.quote: A DPIA does not have to indicate that all risks have been eradicated. But it should help you document them and assess whether or not any remaining risks are justified.

extractions.assertion: DPIAs are legally required for high-risk processing but can also bring broader compliance, financial and reputational benefits.
extractions.quote: DPIAs are a legal requirement for processing that is likely to be high risk. But an effective DPIA can also bring broader compliance, financial and reputational benefits, helping you demonstrate accountability and building trust and engagement with individuals.

extractions.assertion: A DPIA can cover a single processing operation or a group of similar processing operations, and multiple controllers can conduct a joint DPIA.
extractions.quote: A DPIA may cover a single processing operation or a group of similar processing operations. A group of controllers can do a joint DPIA.

extractions.assertion: DPIAs should be embedded into organizational processes and the DPIA outcome should be able to influence organizational plans.
extractions.quote: It's important to embed DPIAs into your organisational processes and ensure the outcome can influence your plans.

extractions.assertion: A DPIA is an ongoing process subject to regular review rather than a one-off exercise.
extractions.quote: A DPIA is not a one-off exercise. You should see it as an ongoing process that is subject to regular review.

extractions.assertion: Processing must be screened for factors pointing to potential widespread or serious impact on individuals to determine if it is likely to result in high risk.
extractions.quote: You must do a DPIA before you begin any type of processing that is "likely to result in a high risk". This means that although you have not yet assessed the actual level of risk, you need to screen for factors that point to the potential for a widespread or serious impact on individuals.

extractions.assertion: The UK GDPR mandates DPIAs specifically for systematic and extensive profiling with significant effects, special category or criminal offence data processing on a large scale, and systematic monitoring of publicly accessible places on large scale.
extractions.quote: In particular, the UK GDPR says you must do a DPIA if you plan to: use systematic and extensive profiling with significant effects; process special category or criminal offence data on a large scale; or systematically monitor publicly accessible places on a large scale.

extractions.assertion: European guidelines define nine criteria of processing operations likely to result in high risk, with most cases involving two or more criteria requiring a DPIA.
extractions.quote: When considering if your processing is likely to result in high risk, you should consider the relevant European guidelines. These define nine criteria of processing operations likely to result in high risk. While the guidelines suggest that, in most cases, any processing operation involving two or more of these criteria requires a DPIA, you may consider in your case that just meeting one criterion could require a DPIA.

extractions.assertion: The ICO requires DPIAs for use of innovative technology combined with criteria from European guidelines.
extractions.quote: The ICO also requires you to do a DPIA if you plan to: use innovative technology (in combination with any of the criteria from the European guidelines)

extractions.assertion: The ICO requires DPIAs for profiling or special category data use in deciding access to services.
extractions.quote: The ICO also requires you to do a DPIA if you plan to: use profiling or special category data to decide on access to services

extractions.assertion: The ICO requires DPIAs for large-scale profiling of individuals.
extractions.quote: The ICO also requires you to do a DPIA if you plan to: profile individuals on a large scale

extractions.assertion: The ICO requires DPIAs for processing biometric data combined with criteria from European guidelines.
extractions.quote: The ICO also requires you to do a DPIA if you plan to: process biometric data (in combination with any of the criteria from the European guidelines)

extractions.assertion: The ICO requires DPIAs for processing genetic data combined with criteria from European guidelines.
extractions.quote: The ICO also requires you to do a DPIA if you plan to: process genetic data (in combination with any of the criteria from the European guidelines)

extractions.assertion: The ICO requires DPIAs for matching or combining datasets from different sources.
extractions.quote: The ICO also requires you to do a DPIA if you plan to: match data or combine datasets from different sources

extractions.assertion: The ICO requires DPIAs for tracking individuals' location or behavior combined with criteria from European guidelines.
extractions.quote: The ICO also requires you to do a DPIA if you plan to: track individuals' location or behaviour (in combination with any of the criteria in the European guidelines)

extractions.assertion: The ICO requires DPIAs for profiling children or targeting marketing or online services at them.
extractions.quote: The ICO also requires you to do a DPIA if you plan to: profile children or target marketing or online services at them

extractions.assertion: The ICO requires DPIAs for processing data that might endanger physical health or safety in the event of a security breach.
extractions.quote: The ICO also requires you to do a DPIA if you plan to: process data that might endanger the individual's physical health or safety in the event of a security breach.

extractions.assertion: Organizations should carefully consider conducting DPIAs for large-scale processing, profiling or monitoring, decisions on service access or opportunities, or processing of sensitive data or vulnerable individuals.
extractions.quote: You should also think carefully about doing a DPIA for any other processing that is large scale, involves profiling or monitoring, decides on access to services or opportunities, or involves sensitive data or vulnerable individuals.

extractions.assertion: A DPIA should begin early in a project lifecycle, before processing starts, and run alongside the planning and development process.
extractions.quote: A DPIA should begin early in the life of a project, before you start your processing, and run alongside the planning and development process.

extractions.assertion: The DPIA process includes seeking data protection officer advice and consulting with individuals and other stakeholders.
extractions.quote: It should include these steps: You must seek the advice of your data protection officer (if you have one). You should also consult with individuals and other stakeholders throughout this process.

extractions.assertion: The DPIA process is designed to be flexible and scalable, allowing organizations to use or adapt sample templates.
extractions.quote: The process is designed to be flexible and scalable. You can use or adapt our sample DPIA template, or create your own.

extractions.assertion: Publishing a DPIA is not a legal requirement under UK GDPR but organizations should actively consider the benefits of publication for demonstrating compliance and building trust.
extractions.quote: Although publishing a DPIA is not a requirement of UK GDPR, you should actively consider the benefits of publication. As well as demonstrating compliance, publication can help engender trust and confidence.

extractions.assertion: Organizations do not need to send every DPIA to the ICO and only a small percentage are expected to be submitted.
extractions.quote: You don't need to send every DPIA to the ICO and we expect the percentage sent to us to be small.

extractions.assertion: The ICO must be consulted if a DPIA identifies a high risk that cannot be mitigated through measures.
extractions.quote: But you must consult the ICO if your DPIA identifies a high risk and you cannot take measures to reduce that risk.

extractions.assertion: Processing cannot begin until the ICO has been consulted about unmitigatable high risks identified in a DPIA.
extractions.quote: You cannot begin the processing until you have consulted us.

extractions.assertion: The ICO generally responds within eight weeks to DPIA consultation requests, with possible extension of six additional weeks in complex cases.
extractions.quote: Once we have the information we need, we will generally respond within eight weeks (although we can extend this by a further six weeks in complex cases).

extractions.assertion: The ICO provides written advice on whether identified risks are acceptable or whether further action is required.
extractions.quote: We will provide you with a written response advising you whether the risks are acceptable, or whether you need to take further action.

extractions.assertion: The ICO may advise against processing or issue formal warnings if it considers processing would breach GDPR.
extractions.quote: In some cases we may advise you not to carry out the processing because we consider it would be in breach of the GDPR. In appropriate cases we may issue a formal warning or take action to ban the processing altogether.

extractions.assertion: A DPIA should be structured clearly, systematically and logically.
extractions.quote: We have: structured the document clearly, systematically and logically

extractions.assertion: A DPIA should be written in plain English with a non-specialist audience in mind, with technical terms and acronyms explained.
extractions.quote: We have: written the DPIA in plain English, with a non-specialist audience in mind, explaining any technical terms and acronyms we have used

extractions.assertion: A DPIA should clearly set out relationships between controllers, processors, data subjects and systems using text and data-flow diagrams.
extractions.quote: We have: set out clearly the relationships between controllers, processors, data subjects and systems, using both text and data-flow diagrams where appropriate

extractions.assertion: A DPIA should clearly explain the specifics of personal data flows between people, systems, organizations and countries.
extractions.quote: We have: ensured that the specifics of any flows of personal data between people, systems, organisations and countries have been clearly explained and presented

extractions.assertion: A DPIA should explain how the organization plans to support the relevant information rights of data subjects.
extractions.quote: We have: explained how we plan to support the relevant information rights of our data subjects

extractions.assertion: A Data Protection Impact Assessment is a tool used to assess and manage data protection risks in processing activities.
extractions.quote: This guidance discusses Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIAs) in detail.

extractions.assertion: DPIAs are relevant to Data Protection Officers and those with specific data protection responsibilities in larger organisations.
extractions.quote: DPOs and those with specific data protection responsibilities in larger organisations are likely to find it useful.

extractions.assertion: The ICO provides guidance on a list of processing operations that are subject to the requirement of conducting a DPIA.
extractions.quote: The guidance has been revised to adopt the European Data Protection Board's 22/2018 opinion on the ICO's list of processing operations subject to the requirement of conducting a DPIA.

extractions.assertion: A DPIA should begin early in the life of a project, before processing starts, and run alongside the planning and development process.
extractions.quote: A DPIA should begin early in the life of a project, before you start your processing, and run alongside the planning and development process.

extractions.assertion: A DPIA process should include seven key steps: identifying the need, describing the processing, considering consultation, assessing necessity and proportionality, identifying and assessing risks, identifying mitigating measures, and signing off and recording outcomes.
extractions.quote: A DPIA should begin early in the life of a project, before you start your processing, and run alongside the planning and development process. It should include these steps: Step 1: identify the need for a DPIA Step 2: describe the processing Step 3: consider consultation Step 4: assess necessity and proportionality Step 5: identify and assess risks Step 6: identify measures to mitigate the risks Step 7: sign off and record outcomes

extractions.assertion: The DPIA process is designed to be flexible and scalable to fit the nature of the project and existing risk management approaches.
extractions.quote: The DPIA process is designed to be flexible and scalable. You can design a process that fits with your existing approach to managing risks and projects, as long as it contains these key elements.

extractions.assertion: If a DPO is present in the organization, the controller must seek the DPO's advice on the DPIA and document it as part of the process.
extractions.quote: If you have a Data Protection Officer (DPO), you must ask for their advice on your DPIA, and document it as part of the process.

extractions.assertion: A processor may be asked to carry out a DPIA on behalf of the controller, but the controller remains responsible for the DPIA.
extractions.quote: You may want to ask a processor to carry out a DPIA on your behalf if they do the relevant processing operation, but again you remain responsible for it.

extractions.assertion: The DPO must provide advice on whether a DPIA is needed, how to conduct it, whether to outsource it, what mitigating measures to take, whether it was done correctly, and whether processing can go ahead.
extractions.quote: The DPO should provide advice on: whether you need to do a DPIA; how you should do a DPIA; whether to outsource the DPIA or do it in-house; what measures and safeguards you can take to mitigate risks; whether you've done the DPIA correctly; and the outcome of the DPIA and whether the processing can go ahead.

extractions.assertion: If major projects involve the use of personal data, it is good practice to conduct a DPIA.
extractions.quote: If you have any major project that involves the use of personal data, it is good practice to do a DPIA.

extractions.assertion: Processing should be screened for factors indicating high-risk processing, such as processing data of vulnerable individuals.
extractions.quote: Otherwise, you need to check whether your processing is on the list of types of processing that automatically require a DPIA. If not, you need to screen for other factors that may indicate it is a type of processing that is likely to result in high risk, such as processing the data of vulnerable individuals.

extractions.assertion: If a DPIA is determined not to be needed, the decision and reasons must be documented, including the DPO's advice.
extractions.quote: If you do this screening and decide a DPIA is not needed, you should document your decision and the reasons for it, including your DPO's advice.

extractions.assertion: A DPIA description of processing must include the nature, scope, context, and purposes of the processing.
extractions.quote: Your description must include "the nature, scope, context and purposes of the processing".

extractions.assertion: The nature of processing in a DPIA should include details about data collection, storage, usage, access, sharing, processors, retention periods, security measures, new technologies, and novel processing types.
extractions.quote: The nature of the processing is what you plan to do with the personal data. This should include, for example: how you collect the data; how you store the data; how you use the data; who has access to the data; who you share the data with; whether you use any processors; retention periods; security measures; whether you are using any new technologies; whether you are using any novel types of processing

extractions.assertion: The scope of processing should include details about the nature, volume, variety, sensitivity, extent, frequency, duration of processing, number of data subjects, and geographical area covered.
extractions.quote: The scope of the processing is what the processing covers. This should include, for example: the nature of the personal data; the volume and variety of the personal data; the sensitivity of the personal data; the extent and frequency of the processing; the duration of the processing; the number of data subjects involved; and the geographical area covered.

extractions.assertion: The context of processing should include the source of data, relationship with individuals, individual control over data, whether individuals expect the processing, inclusion of children or vulnerable people, previous experience with such processing, technological advances, public concerns, and compliance with codes of conduct or certification schemes.
extractions.quote: The context of the processing is the wider picture, including internal and external factors which might affect expectations or impact. This might include, for example: the source of the data; the nature of your relationship with the individuals; how far individuals have control over their data; how far individuals are likely to expect the processing; whether these individuals include children or other vulnerable people; any previous experience of this type of processing; any relevant advances in technology or security; any current issues of public concern

extractions.assertion: The purpose of processing should include legitimate interests, intended outcomes for individuals, and expected benefits for the controller or society.
extractions.quote: The purpose of the processing is the reason why you want to process the personal data. This should include: your legitimate interests, where relevant; the intended outcome for individuals; and the expected benefits for you or for society as a whole.

extractions.assertion: Views of individuals or their representatives should be sought and documented unless there is a good reason not to.
extractions.quote: You should seek and document the views of individuals (or their representatives) unless there is a good reason not to.

extractions.assertion: Consultation may be inappropriate if it would compromise commercial confidentiality, undermine security, or be disproportionate or impracticable.
extractions.quote: For example, you may be able to demonstrate that consultation would compromise commercial confidentiality, undermine security, or be disproportionate or impracticable.

extractions.assertion: If DPIA decision differs from the views of individuals, the reasons for disregarding their views must be documented.
extractions.quote: If your DPIA decision differs from the views of individuals, you need to document your reasons for disregarding their views.

extractions.assertion: Data processor contracts should require processors to assist with providing information and assistance for the DPIA.
extractions.quote: Your contracts with processors should require them to assist.

extractions.assertion: Legal advice or advice from independent experts such as IT experts, sociologists or ethicists should be considered where appropriate, though there are no specific requirements to do so.
extractions.quote: We also recommend you consider seeking legal advice or advice from other independent experts such as IT experts, sociologists or ethicists where appropriate. However, there are no specific requirements to do so.

extractions.assertion: When assessing necessity and proportionality, considerations should include whether plans achieve the intended purpose and whether alternative reasonable ways exist to achieve the same result.
extractions.quote: You should consider: Do your plans help to achieve your purpose? Is there any other reasonable way to achieve the same result?

extractions.assertion: Data protection compliance measures are a good measure of necessity and proportionality and should include lawful basis, prevention of function creep, data quality, data minimisation, privacy information provision, support for individual rights, processor compliance measures, and safeguards for international transfers.
extractions.quote: The Article 29 guidelines also say you should include how you ensure data protection compliance, which are a good measure of necessity and proportionality. In particular, you should include relevant details of: your lawful basis for the processing; how you will prevent function creep; how you intend to ensure data quality; how you intend to ensure data minimisation; how you intend to provide privacy information to individuals; how you implement and support individuals' rights; measures to ensure your processors comply; and safeguards for international transfers.

extractions.assertion: Risk assessment should consider potential impacts on individuals including inability to exercise rights, inability to access services, loss of control over personal data, discrimination, identity theft, fraud, financial loss, reputational damage, physical harm, loss of confidentiality, and re-identification of pseudonymised data.
extractions.quote: Consider the potential impact on individuals and any harm or damage your processing may cause - whether physical, emotional or material. In particular, look at whether the processing could contribute to: inability to exercise rights (including but not limited to privacy rights); inability to access services or opportunities; loss of control over the use of personal data; discrimination; identity theft or fraud; financial loss; reputational damage; physical harm; loss of confidentiality; re-identification of pseudonymised data; or any other significant economic or social disadvantage

extractions.assertion: Security risks assessment should include sources of risk and potential impact of each type of breach including illegitimate access, modification, or loss of personal data.
extractions.quote: You should include an assessment of the security risks, including sources of risk and the potential impact of each type of breach (including illegitimate access to, modification of or loss of personal data).

extractions.assertion: To assess whether a risk is high risk, both the likelihood and severity of possible harm must be considered.
extractions.quote: To assess whether the risk is a high risk, you need to consider both the likelihood and severity of the possible harm.

extractions.assertion: Harm does not have to be inevitable to qualify as high risk; it must be more than remote, but any significant possibility of very serious harm may still qualify as high risk.
extractions.quote: Harm does not have to be inevitable to qualify as a risk or a high risk. It must be more than remote, but any significant possibility of very serious harm may still be enough to qualify as a high risk.

extractions.assertion: A high probability of widespread but more minor harm may still count as high risk.
extractions.quote: Equally, a high probability of widespread but more minor harm may still count as high risk.

extractions.assertion: Risk assessment must be objective.
extractions.quote: You must make an objective assessment of the risks.

extractions.assertion: A structured matrix considering likelihood and severity of risks is a helpful tool for assessing risk.
extractions.quote: It is helpful to use a structured matrix to think about likelihood and severity of risks

extractions.assertion: Corporate risks such as regulatory action, reputational damage, or loss of public trust should be considered when assessing risks.
extractions.quote: You may also want to consider your own corporate risks, such as the impact of regulatory action, reputational damage or loss of public trust.

extractions.assertion: Mitigating measures should include the source of each identified risk and options for reducing that risk such as limiting data collection, reducing processing scope, reducing retention periods, improving security, staff training, anonymisation, pseudonymisation, and data-sharing agreements.
extractions.quote: Against each risk identified, record its source. You should then consider options for reducing that risk. For example: deciding not to collect certain types of data; reducing the scope of the processing; reducing retention periods; taking additional technological security measures; training staff to ensure risks are anticipated and managed; anonymising or pseudonymising data where possible; writing internal guidance or processes to avoid risks; using a different technology; putting clear data-sharing agreements into place; making changes to privacy notices; offering individuals the chance to opt out where appropriate; or implementing new systems to help individuals to exercise their rights.

extractions.assertion: The DPO should be asked for advice on mitigating measures, and whether each measure would reduce or eliminate the risk should be recorded.
extractions.quote: You should ask your DPO for advice. Record whether the measure would reduce or eliminate the risk.

extractions.assertion: Costs and benefits of mitigating measures should be considered when deciding whether to implement them.
extractions.quote: You can take into account the costs and benefits of each measure when deciding whether or not they are appropriate.

extractions.assertion: The DPIA conclusion should record additional measures, whether each risk is eliminated/reduced/accepted, overall residual risk level, and whether ICO consultation is needed.
extractions.quote: You should then record: what additional measures you plan to take; whether each risk has been eliminated, reduced, or accepted; the overall level of 'residual risk' after taking additional measures; and whether you need to consult the ICO.

extractions.assertion: Not every risk must be eliminated; some risks, even high risks, may be acceptable given the benefits of processing and mitigation difficulties.
extractions.quote: You do not always have to eliminate every risk. You may decide that some risks, and even a high risk, are acceptable given the benefits of the processing and the difficulties of mitigation.

extractions.assertion: If high risk remains after assessment, ICO consultation is required before processing can proceed.
extractions.quote: However, if there is still a high risk, you need to consult the ICO before you can go ahead with the processing.

extractions.assertion: DPO advice on whether processing is compliant and can go ahead should be sought and documented as part of sign-off; if advice is not followed, reasons must be recorded.
extractions.quote: As part of the sign-off process, you should seek and document DPO advice on whether the processing is compliant and can go ahead. If you decide not to follow their advice, you need to record your reasons.

extractions.assertion: Reasons for going against the views of individuals or other consultees should be recorded.
extractions.quote: You should also record any reasons for going against the views of individuals or other consultees.

extractions.assertion: DPIA outcomes must be integrated into project plans with identified action points and responsible parties.
extractions.quote: You must integrate the outcomes of your DPIA into your project plans. You should identify any action points and who is responsible for implementing them.

extractions.assertion: DPIA performance should be monitored on an ongoing basis.
extractions.quote: You should monitor the ongoing performance of the DPIA.

extractions.assertion: If high risk is accepted because mitigation is impossible or costs are too high, ICO consultation is mandatory before processing proceeds.
extractions.quote: If you have decided to accept a high risk, either because it is not possible to mitigate or because the costs of mitigation are too high, you must consult the ICO before you go ahead with the processing.

extractions.assertion: Publishing a DPIA is good practice to foster trust and improve individuals' ability to exercise their rights.
extractions.quote: To aid transparency and accountability, it is good practice to publish your DPIA. This could help foster trust in your processing activities, and improve individuals' ability to exercise their rights.

extractions.assertion: If publication of a DPIA may reveal commercially sensitive information or undermine security, redaction, removal of details, or publication of a summary should be considered.
extractions.quote: If you are concerned that publication may reveal commercially sensitive information, undermine security or cause other risks, you should consider whether you can redact (black out) or remove sensitive details, or publish a summary.

extractions.assertion: A DPIA must be kept under review and may need to be repeated if there is a substantial change to the nature, scope, context, or purposes of processing.
extractions.quote: You need to keep your DPIA under review. You may need to repeat it if there is a substantial change to the nature, scope, context or purposes of your processing.

extractions.assertion: Processing operations involving innovative technology or novel applications of existing technologies, including AI, require a DPIA when combined with other criteria from the EDPB guidelines.
extractions.quote: A DPIA is required for any intended processing operation(s) involving innovative use of technologies (or applying new technological and/or organisational solutions) when combined with any other criterion from WP248rev01.

extractions.assertion: Automated decision-making about an individual's access to products, services, opportunities, or benefits requires a DPIA.
extractions.quote: Decisions about an individual's access to a product, service, opportunity or benefit which are based to any extent on automated decision-making (including profiling) or involves the processing of special-category data.

extractions.assertion: Large-scale profiling of individuals requires a DPIA.
extractions.quote: Any profiling of individuals on a large scale

extractions.assertion: Processing of biometric data for the purpose of uniquely identifying an individual requires a DPIA when combined with other criteria.
extractions.quote: A DPIA is required for any intended processing operation(s) involving biometric data for the purpose of uniquely identifying an individual, when combined with any other criterion from WP248rev01

extractions.assertion: Processing of genetic data, except by individual GPs or health professionals providing direct healthcare, requires a DPIA when combined with other criteria.
extractions.quote: A DPIA is required for any intended processing operation(s) involving genetic data when combined with any other criterion from WP248rev01

extractions.assertion: Data matching involving combining, comparing, or matching personal data from multiple sources requires a DPIA.
extractions.quote: Combining, comparing or matching personal data obtained from multiple sources

extractions.assertion: Processing personal data not obtained directly from the data subject, where the controller relies on Article 14.5(b) impossibility or disproportionate effort, requires a DPIA when combined with other criteria.
extractions.quote: A DPIA is required for any intended processing operation(s) involving where the controller is relying on Article 14.5(b) when combined with any other criterion from WP248rev01

extractions.assertion: Tracking an individual's geolocation or behaviour, including online tracking, requires a DPIA when combined with other criteria.
extractions.quote: A DPIA is required for any intended processing operation involving geolocation data when combined with any other criterion from WP248rev01

extractions.assertion: Processing that poses a risk of physical harm to individuals in case of personal data breach requires a DPIA.
extractions.quote: Where the processing is of such a nature that a personal data breach could jeopardise the [physical] health or safety of individuals.

extractions.assertion: Processing personal data of children or vulnerable individuals for marketing, profiling, automated decision-making, or offering online services requires a DPIA.
extractions.quote: The use of the personal data of children or other vulnerable individuals for marketing purposes, profiling or other automated decision-making, or if you intend to offer online services directly to children.

extractions.assertion: Organizations have an overriding obligation under Article 35(1) to assess any proposed processing operation against the requirement to complete DPIAs regardless of provided high-risk lists.
extractions.quote: In any event, this list does not affect your overriding obligation in Article 35(1), which is to assess any proposed processing operation against the requirement to complete DPIAs.

extractions.assertion: The ICO considers it best practice to conduct a DPIA whether or not the processing is likely to result in high risk.
extractions.quote: The ICO also considers it best practice to do a DPIA, whether or not the processing is likely to result in a high risk.

extractions.assertion: A data protection impact assessment is required when processing is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of data subjects.
extractions.quote: If you have determined that the processing is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of data subjects, you must carry out a data protection impact assessment (DPIA) for each processing operation.

extractions.assertion: A DPIA allows the controller to develop privacy-friendly personal data processing operations and products, assess the impact on privacy, and demonstrate respect for GDPR fundamental principles.
extractions.quote: The DPIA allows the controller to: develop privacy friendly personal data processing operations and products, assess the impact on the privacy of data subjects, demonstrate that the fundamental principles of the GDPR are respected.

extractions.assertion: Processing of genetic data requires a DPIA when combined with at least one additional criterion from Article 29 working party guidelines, except for healthcare professionals providing healthcare services.
extractions.quote: Processing activities that rely on genetic data as defined under GDPR article 4 (13) in conjunction with at least one other criteria from the article 29 working party guidelines (WP248 rev. 01), except for healthcare professionals when providing healthcare services

extractions.assertion: Processing activities using biometric data for identification of data subjects require a DPIA when combined with at least one additional criterion from Article 29 working party guidelines.
