extractions.quote: Processing activities that include biometric data as defined under GDPR article 4(14) and have as a purpose identification of data subjects in conjunction with at least one other criteria from the article 29 working party guidelines (WP248 rev. 01)

extractions.assertion: A DPIA is required for regular and systematic monitoring of employee activities that might produce legal effects or significantly affect employees.
extractions.quote: Processing activities that consist of or include regular and systematic monitoring of employee activities - provided that they might produce legal effects concerning the employees or similarly significantly affects them

extractions.assertion: A DPIA is required for systematic tracking of natural persons' positions.
extractions.quote: Processing activities that consist in systematic tracking of natural persons position

extractions.assertion: Processing activities on files containing personal data of the entire national population require a DPIA unless one has already been carried out as part of a general impact assessment.
extractions.quote: Processing activities on files that might contain personal data of the whole national population provided that such a DPIA has not already been carried out as part of a general impact assessment in the context of the adoption of that legal basis

extractions.assertion: Rights and freedoms of natural persons refer mainly to data protection and privacy, but also include other fundamental rights such as freedom of speech, freedom of thought, and freedom of movement.
extractions.quote: The reference to the rights and freedoms of natural persons refers mainly to data protection and the protection of privacy but also, where appropriate, to other fundamental rights, such as freedom of speech, freedom of thought, freedom of movement, prohibition of discrimination, the right to freedom and freedom of conscience and religion.

extractions.assertion: A DPIA is required for systematic and extensive evaluation of personal aspects based on automated processing and profiling that produces legal effects or significantly affects data subjects.
extractions.quote: a systematic and extensive evaluation of personal aspects relating to natural persons which is based on automated processing, including profiling, and on which decisions are based that produce legal effects concerning the natural person or similarly significantly affect the natural person

extractions.assertion: A DPIA is required for large-scale processing of special categories of data or personal data relating to criminal convictions and offences.
extractions.quote: processing on a large scale of special categories of data referred to in Article 9(1) of the GDPR, or of personal data relating to criminal convictions and offences referred to in Article 10 of the GDPR

extractions.assertion: A DPIA is required for systematic monitoring of a publicly accessible area on a large scale.
extractions.quote: a systematic monitoring of a publicly accessible area on a large scale

extractions.assertion: A DPIA may be carried out on a voluntary basis to identify and manage risks even if they are minor.
extractions.quote: A DPIA may also be carried out on a voluntary basis in order to identify and deal as effectively as possible with the risks, even if they are minor, to the rights and freedoms of individuals.

extractions.assertion: A DPIA may relate to a single data processing operation or can evaluate several similar processing operations in terms of nature, scope, context, purposes and risks.
extractions.quote: A DPIA may relate to a single data processing operation and can also be used to evaluate several similar processing operations in terms of nature, scope, context, purposes and risks.

extractions.assertion: A DPIA must include a systematic description of the processing including nature, scope, context, personal data concerned, recipients, retention period, and identification of assets.
extractions.quote: A systematic description of the processing is provided [article 35, paragraph 7, point a)]: The nature, scope, context and the of the processing are taken into account (recital 90) The personal data concerned, the recipients and the period for which the personal data will be kept are specified; A functional description of the processing operation is provided; The assets on which the personal data are based (hardware, software, networks, individuals, paper documents or paper transmission channels) are identified

extractions.assertion: A DPIA must assess the necessity and proportionality of processing, including measures to ensure compliance and respect for GDPR principles.
extractions.quote: The necessity and the proportionality are assessed [article 35, paragraph 7, point b)]: The measures envisaged to ensure compliance with the Regulation are determined, [article 35, paragraph 7, point d), and recital 90] taking into account: Measures contributing to the respect of the principles of proportionality and necessity of processing

extractions.assertion: A DPIA must address the rights of data subjects including information provision, right of access, right to rectification, and right to erasure.
extractions.quote: Measures contributing to the rights of the data subjects: Information provided to the data subject (articles 12, 13 and 14); Right of access and right to data portability (articles 15 and 20) Right to rectification and right to erasure (articles 16, 17 and 19) Right to restriction of processing and right to object (articles 18, 19 and 21)

extractions.assertion: A DPIA must assess the origin, nature, particularity and gravity of risks to the rights and freedoms of data subjects.
extractions.quote: The risks to the rights and freedoms of data subjects are managed [article 35, paragraph 7, point c)]: The origin, the nature, the particularity and the gravity of the risks are assessed (recital 84)

extractions.assertion: A DPIA must identify potential impacts on data subject rights in case of illegitimate access, unwanted modification, or disappearance of data.
extractions.quote: Potential impacts on the rights and freedoms of data subjects are identified in case of events such as illegitimate access to data, an unwanted modification of data or their disappearance

extractions.assertion: A DPIA must involve the opinion of the Data Protection Officer and, where appropriate, the point of view of data subjects or their representatives.
extractions.quote: Interested parties are involved: The opinion of the DPO is obtained (article 35, paragraph 2); The point of view of the data subjects or their representatives are gathered, where appropriate (article 35, paragraph 9).

extractions.assertion: The data controller must consult the CNPD when identified risks cannot be sufficiently addressed and residual risks remain high.
extractions.quote: The data controller must consult the CNPD in cases where the identified risks cannot be sufficiently addressed (i.e. the residual risks remains high).

extractions.assertion: Processing may only be carried out after implementing the recommendations in the CNPD's opinion following prior consultation.
extractions.quote: Processing may only be carried out after implementing the recommandations in the opinion of the CNPD.

extractions.assertion: Prior consultation requests must address all admissibility criteria in the CNPD form, and missing criteria may result in suspension of DPIA processing.
extractions.quote: It is imperative that the impact assessment addresses all the admissibility criteria in section "2. Criteria for an acceptable DPIA" of the form. Missing criteria may result in the suspension of the processing of the DPIA until the missing information is obtained from the data controller.

extractions.assertion: The CNPD provides written advice within up to eight weeks of receiving a prior consultation request, with possible extension of six weeks for complex processing.
extractions.quote: It provides written advice to the controller and, where applicable to the processor within period of up to eight weeks of receipt of the request for consultation. That period may be extended by six weeks, taking into account the complexity of the intended processing.

extractions.assertion: Processing operations previously authorized by the CNPD do not require a new DPIA if they have not changed since implementation.
extractions.quote: If the processing operations have been authorized by the CNPD and if they have not changed since their implementation, it is not mandatory to carry out a DPIA.

extractions.assertion: Any processing operations that have changed since authorization and are likely to result in high risk require a DPIA, even if previously authorized.
extractions.quote: But, this also means that any processing operations where the conditions (scope, purposes, personal data collected, identity of data controllers or recipients, data retention period, technical and organizational measures, etc.) have changed since the authorization was issued by the CNPD and are likely to result in a high risk, require a DPIA.

extractions.assertion: A DPIA should be reevaluated when there is a change in the risk represented by the processing operation due to evolution of technology, use of data for different purposes, or organizational context changes.
extractions.quote: Moreover, a DPIA may be necessary as a result of a risk evolution arising from processing operations, for example due to the use of new technology or the use of personal data for different purposes. Processing operations may evolve rapidly and new vulnerabilities may emerge.

extractions.assertion: A DPIA is an ongoing process for managing risks, not a one-time exercise, and must be reevaluated when the risk represented by the processing operation changes.
extractions.quote: Carrying out a DPIA is not a one-time exercise. It is an an on-going process that helps you to manage the risks resulting from a processing. It is important to reevaluate the DPIA when there is a change of the risk represented by the processing operation.

extractions.assertion: Publishing a DPIA is not legally required but controllers should consider publishing to foster trust, demonstrate accountability and transparency.
extractions.quote: Publishing a DPIA is not a legal requirement of the GDPR. It is left upon the controller ́s decision. However, data controllers should consider publishing their DPIA, or perhaps part of their DPIA. The purpose of such a process would be to help foster trust in the controller's processing operations, and demonstrate accountability and transparency.

extractions.assertion: A controller must consult with the Commissioner prior to processing if a data protection impact assessment indicates that the processing would result in high risk without mitigating measures.
extractions.quote: The controller shall consult the Commissioner prior to processing where a data protection impact assessment under Article 35 indicates that the processing would result in a high risk in the absence of measures taken by the controller to mitigate the risk.

extractions.assertion: When a data protection impact assessment indicates high-risk processing, the DPIA itself becomes a mandatory consultation trigger for engaging with the Commissioner.
extractions.quote: The controller shall consult the Commissioner prior to processing where a data protection impact assessment under Article 35 indicates that the processing would result in a high risk

extractions.assertion: The Commissioner must provide written advice within eight weeks of receiving a consultation request, or extend that period by up to six weeks if the processing is complex.
extractions.quote: the Commissioner shall, within period of up to eight weeks of receipt of the request for consultation, provide written advice to the controller and, where applicable to the processor. That period may be extended by six weeks, taking into account the complexity of the intended processing.

extractions.assertion: Controllers must provide the Commissioner with specific information when consulting about high-risk processing, including responsibilities of parties involved, processing purposes and means, protective measures, data protection officer contact details, and the DPIA itself.
extractions.quote: When consulting the Commissioner pursuant to paragraph 1, the controller shall provide the Commissioner with: (a)where applicable, the respective responsibilities of the controller, joint controllers and processors involved in the processing; (b)the purposes and means of the intended processing; (c)the measures and safeguards provided to protect the rights and freedoms of data subjects; (d)where applicable, the contact details of the data protection officer; (e)the data protection impact assessment provided for in Article 35; and (f)any other information requested by the Commissioner.

extractions.assertion: Relevant government authorities must consult the Commissioner during preparation of legislative or regulatory measures that relate to processing.
extractions.quote: The relevant authority must consult the Commissioner during the preparation of a proposal for a legislative measure to be adopted by Parliament, the National Assembly for Wales, the Scottish Parliament or the Northern Ireland Assembly, or of a regulatory measure based on such a legislative measure, which relates to processing.

extractions.assertion: Prior consultation with the ICO is required when a DPIA identifies a high risk that cannot be reduced through mitigating measures.
extractions.quote: If you have carried out a DPIA that identifies a high risk and you cannot do anything to reduce it, prior consultation with the ICO is required under UK GDPR.

extractions.assertion: Organizations must not proceed with processing until after consulting the ICO when a high residual risk has been identified.
extractions.quote: You cannot go ahead with the processing until you have consulted us. The focus is on the 'residual risk' after you have taken any mitigating measures.

extractions.assertion: ICO consultation is not required if a DPIA identified high risk but mitigating measures have reduced it to no longer be high.
extractions.quote: If your DPIA identified a high risk but you have done things to reduce the risk so it is no longer high, you need not consult us.

extractions.assertion: A DPIA submission to the ICO must include descriptions of roles and responsibilities of joint controllers or processors, processing purposes and methods, protective measures and safeguards, DPO contact details, and a copy of the DPIA itself.
extractions.quote: You must include: a description of the respective roles and responsibilities of any joint controllers or processors; the purposes and methods of the intended processing; the measures and safeguards taken to protect individuals; contact details of your DPO (if you have one); and a copy of the DPIA.

extractions.assertion: The ICO will acknowledge receipt of a DPIA submission and notify the applicant within 10 days whether the DPIA has been accepted for prior consultation.
extractions.quote: We will write to you to within 10 days to let you know if we have accepted your DPIA for prior consultation. We will explain our reasoning.

extractions.assertion: The ICO assesses not only the documented risks in a DPIA but also the complete submission, prior contact history, processing context, controller-processor relationships, and evidence of Data Protection Principles compliance.
extractions.quote: If we accept your DPIA, we don't just look at the risks you documented. We consider all of your submission - your DPIA documentation and any further information you provided - along with any prior contact you may have had with our office.

extractions.assertion: The ICO will provide advice on prior consultation cases within eight weeks of receipt, extendable to a maximum of 14 weeks for complex cases.
extractions.quote: Where we provide advice under the prior consultation process, we will get back to you within eight weeks of receipt of your DPIA. In complex cases, we can extend this to a maximum of 14 weeks.

extractions.assertion: The ICO may issue official warnings if concerned that intended processing is likely to contravene UK GDPR.
extractions.quote: In some circumstances, we may also issue an official warning, a new corrective power under UK GDPR, alongside any advice we provide. We will issue warnings where we are concerned that your intended processing is likely to contravene UK GDPR.

extractions.assertion: The ICO may impose limitations or bans on intended processing when it has significant concerns.
extractions.quote: If we have more significant concerns, we may impose a limitation or ban on your intended processing.

extractions.assertion: A data controller must consult the Supervisory Authority when a DPIA indicates that processing would result in high risk to data protection rights and mitigating measures cannot eliminate the residual risks.
extractions.quote: Where a data controller carries out a Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA), which indicates that the intended processing would result in a high risk to the data protection rights of individuals in the absence of mitigating measures, the controller shall consult the Supervisory Authority.

extractions.assertion: Prior consultation is mandatory when a controller proposes to engage in a type of processing that has been prescribed in regulations under Section 84(9) of the Data Protection Act 2018.
extractions.quote: Prior consultation with the DPC will also be mandatory where the controller proposes to engage in a type of processing that has been prescribed in regulations in accordance with Section84(9) of Data Protection Act 2018.

extractions.assertion: Controllers must submit the DPIA, documentation of responsibilities between controllers and processors, processing purposes and means, protective measures and safeguards, and DPO contact details when seeking prior consultation.
extractions.quote: The Data Protection Impact Assessment and any ancillary documents; The respective responsibilities of the controller, joint controllers and processors involved in the processing, in particular for processing within a group of undertakings; The purposes and means of the intended processing; The measures and safeguards provided to protect the rights and freedoms of data subjects under the GDPR; The contact details of the Data Protection Officer (if applicable)

extractions.assertion: The DPC must identify and clarify the respective responsibilities of controllers, joint controllers, and processors involved in the processing during prior consultation assessment.
extractions.quote: The respective responsibilities of the controller, joint controllers and processors involved in the processing, in particular for processing within a group of undertakings

extractions.assertion: The DPC will respond to a prior consultation submission within eight weeks if the processing would infringe GDPR provisions or risks are insufficiently identified or mitigated.
extractions.quote: The DPC will respond to a submission for statutory prior consultation within a period of up to eight weeks, where it appears that the intended processing would infringe the provisions of the GDPR or Data Protection Act, or that the controller has insufficiently identified or mitigated the potential risks.

extractions.assertion: The DPC response period may be extended by up to six weeks to account for the complexity of the proposed processing.
extractions.quote: The period for responding may be extended by a period of up to six weeks, taking into account the complexity of the proposed processing.

extractions.assertion: Each data protection authority issues a list of processing operations that require a data protection impact assessment, following an EDPB opinion.
extractions.quote: Each data protection authority issues a list of the kind of processing operations which are subject to the requirement for a data protection impact assessment (DPIA), following an EDPB opinion (Art. 35(4) GDPR).

extractions.assertion: Data protection authorities may establish a list of processing operations for which no DPIA is required.
extractions.quote: Data protection authority may also establish a list of the kind of processing operations for which no DPIA is required (Art. 35(5) GDPR).

extractions.assertion: Data controllers are required to carry out a DPIA before any processing that is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of individuals.
extractions.quote: Data controllers need to carry out a DPIA before any processing likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of individuals.

extractions.assertion: If risks identified in a DPIA cannot be mitigated by appropriate measures, the controller must consult the Data Protection Authority before proceeding with the processing.
extractions.quote: If such risks cannot be mitigated by appropriate measures, the controller needs to consult the Data Protection Authority (DPA) before proceeding.

extractions.assertion: DPIAs help organizations identify and manage risks to people's personal data.
extractions.quote: Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIA) help organizations identify and manage risks to people's personal data.

extractions.assertion: Data Protection Authorities adopt lists specifying which types of processing activities require or do not require a DPIA.
extractions.quote: DPAs also adopt lists of the kind of processing activities for which a DPIA is or is not required, which are subject to opinions of the Board.
